title: The Denver Broncos are embracing their bond with anime horse girls
summary: The football team and "Umamusume" will collaborate on Dec. 6 when they play the Miami Dolphins.
content: Last season, the Denver Broncos were adopted by the anime horse girl community centered around “Umamusume: Pretty Derby.” And after a year of it being a one-sided relationship, the Broncos are now reciprocating with a special day collaboration on Dec. 6 when they play the Miami Dolphins. Sorry, I need more context “Umamusume” centers around anime girls with the ears, tails and racing capabilities of horses. While the franchise started with a mobile video game, it has since expanded to become an animated series, a graphic novel and even a stage play. During last year’s breakout Broncos season , “Umamusume” fans started to make highlight reels of Broncos games set to the theme song of the Japanese media franchise. The tradition has continued, with some fans even dressing up as horse girls and attending games. And now, the connection will be stronger than ever. What to expect at the ‘Umamusume’ booth “Umamusume” will be running a booth at the East Rock Garden near Gate 8 of Empower Field at Mile High, which will be available to any fans, regardless of whether they have a ticket to the game. The booth will feature life-sized cardboard cutouts of the characters Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen wearing Broncos uniforms. Huddle up, Trainers! Gold Ship's got a special collab announcement for you! Watch the video to see what's cooking! #Umamusume pic.twitter.com/ySkF3BBzu0 — Umamusume: Pretty Derby (@umamusume_eng) November 19, 2026 As per the “Umamusume” wiki, Gold Ship is an “unpredictable firebrand born with an extra helping of free spirit” — kind of like Nik Bonitto bursting into the backfield. Mejiro McQueen “is a long-distance runner who is the envy of her peers” — a real Marvin Mims Jr. (Ed. note: If these are incorrect, take it up with editor Andy Kenney.) Additionally, “trainers” (that’s you!) who visit will also receive a postcard with the same illustration of Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen, as well as a rally flag featuring a “special illustration of Gold Ship scoring a touchdown in a Broncos uniform.” The Broncos are currently 7-2 and next play on Thanksgiving Day against the Las Vegas Raiders.
